subject.title: feature: Add new functionality to connect options

question: Should the Windows companion support a constrained managed port-forward transport for commands such as `kubectl port-forward`, or expose unrestricted connection lifecycle scripts?
rationale: Both options satisfy the reported topology, but they create materially different local code-execution, persistence, support, and credential boundaries that require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Constrained port-forward profile
options.body: Model an executable and structured arguments with explicit consent, readiness, deduplicated reconnect behavior, process ownership, cleanup, and redacted diagnostics.

options.title: Generic lifecycle scripts
options.body: Allow arbitrary start/stop shell commands and accept the broader command-execution and configuration surface.

options.title: External process only
options.body: Keep the app limited to direct URL and SSH modes and require users to manage `kubectl port-forward` outside the companion.

recommendation.title: Constrained port-forward profile
recommendation.body: Model an executable and structured arguments with explicit consent, readiness, deduplicated reconnect behavior, process ownership, cleanup, and redacted diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active onboarding tracking context and recently reopened this issue, while the implementation decision can be reviewed with the connection-history owners.
